normal_form_scope_precision.finite_support_argument: A hypothetical equality of a finite written graph word to1 in the presentation is a finite product of conjugates of defining relators in the free product of vertex groups and edge letters. Collect the finitely many word/conjugator/relator vertices and edges. Add the finite union of unique T-paths joining their vertices. This gives a finite connected graph Y with T intersect Y a maximal subtree, and contains every relator in that finite equality witness, including every tree-edge relator used. Consequently the same written equality holds in pi1(G|Y,T intersect Y). Every internal reducedness test for the original word uses the same vertex/edge groups and monomorphisms, hence remains true in Y. The proved finite-edge normal form contradicts that equality. This establishes the arbitrary-graph nonidentity implication used here without assuming injectivity of a finite subgraph fundamental group into the full one. Finite word reduction/existence follows by inserting finite T-paths and cancelling the finitely many forbidden backtracks; edge count strictly decreases at each cancellation.
